resources.string: Choose how your times are calculated. Nothing is chosen for you, and you can change any of this later.
Each method sets how dawn (Fajr) and night (Isha) are judged. Different communities follow different methods, so times can differ by a few minutes.

If you do not know which method your community follows, ask your local masjid. You can change it here later, and the app will never change it for you. To continue now, you can start with the Muslim World League method and confirm it later.
This sets how the afternoon (Asr) prayer is worked out, and can move Asr later in the day.
Times are calculated for one city. Search the offline list, or use your location to suggest the nearest one. Choose a country first to browse its cities.
Optional. Suggests the nearest city from your approximate location, used once and never saved.
Location permission was not granted. Search for a city instead.
Couldn\'t get your location. Search for a city instead.
Change your city or how times are calculated. Nothing changes until you save, and the app never changes these for you.

If your local masjid announces a slightly different time, you can move each prayer by whole minutes. These are your own adjustments, shown separately from the calculated time; they never change the calculation method or its settings, and clearing them brings back the raw time.
Fajr 18°, Isha 17°. Used widely in Europe and by many communities.
Fajr 18°, Isha 18°. Common in South Asia, including Bangladesh and Pakistan.
Fajr 18.5°, Isha 90 minutes after Maghrib. Used in Saudi Arabia.
Fajr 19.5°, Isha 17.5°. Used in Egypt and parts of Africa.
Fajr 18°, Isha 18°, with a seasonal adjustment at high latitudes. Used by some communities in the UK and North America.
Fajr and Isha 18.2°. Used in the Gulf region.
Fajr 18°, Isha 90 minutes after Maghrib. Used in Qatar.
Fajr 20°, Isha 18°. Used in Singapore and parts of Southeast Asia.
Fajr 15°, Isha 15°. Used by some communities in North America.
Shadow length 2×, which places Asr later in the day.

At high latitudes the sun may not reach the Fajr or Isha angle, so this rule limits how far those times can go. It changes nothing at most latitudes. If you are not sure, the middle of the night is the most permissive limit. The Moonsighting Committee method does not use this rule, and applies its own seasonal adjustment instead.
Fajr is never earlier, and Isha never later, than the middle of the night.
Fajr is no earlier than the last seventh of the night; Isha no later than the end of the first seventh.
The limit is the fraction of the night that this method\'s Fajr and Isha angles imply.
Calculated times vary by method, city, date and local authority, so a nearby masjid may announce slightly different times.
Not used by this method: it applies its own seasonal adjustment at high latitude instead.
Fajr here comes from the high-latitude rule instead of true dawn: on this date at this latitude, true dawn either is not reached or falls beyond this rule\'s limit.
Isha here comes from the high-latitude rule instead of true dusk: on this date at this latitude, true dusk either is not reached or falls beyond this rule\'s limit.
Fajr and Isha here come from the high-latitude rule instead of true dawn and dusk: on this date at this latitude, they either are not reached or fall beyond this rule\'s limit.
Times cannot be calculated for %1$s on this date: at this latitude and time of year the sun neither rises nor sets.
Hijri date: calculated, on the Umm al-Qura convention
Calculated, so it can differ by a day or more from the date your country or community announces. This is not a confirmed local sighting.
Your Hijri date is showing one day earlier.
Your Hijri date is showing one day later.
Reminders are off unless you turn on a prayer here, one at a time. The app asks for notification permission only after you turn one on.
No reminders are on. Everything else in the app works without them.
No reminder is sent between these times, in your chosen city\'s local time. A reminder inside the window is skipped, not delayed.
The start and end are the same time, so this window suppresses nothing. Choose different times.
Notifications show a neutral message only. Your prayer names and times never appear on the lock screen.
Android decides when a reminder is delivered. Exact timing depends on the operating system and battery policy, so it may arrive later than the calculated time.

You will get a notification at the time you chose for that prayer. Android asks for permission next. Notifications show a neutral message only, never a prayer name or time, and exact delivery depends on the operating system and battery policy. Everything else works without them.
Notifications are turned off for this app, so reminders cannot be delivered. Everything else still works. You can allow notifications later in system settings.
The reminders you turn on, at the times you chose. Notifications show a neutral message.
Sign in with Google or Apple to carry your settings and tasbih total to another device. Prayer times, qibla, tasbih and reminders still work without an account.
This permanently deletes your account and the settings and tasbih total saved on the server. Your city, prayer times, reminders and tasbih stay on this device.
Could not check sign-in. You can continue without an account.
Could not sign out. Check your connection and try again.
Could not prepare your data. Check your connection and try again.
Could not delete your account. Check your connection and try again.
The city list could not be read. Reinstall the app, or report the problem.
Counts whatever you name. The app bundles no text of its own and attributes none — the label is your own words, kept on this device.
Type a label and set a target to start counting.
Target reached. Reset to count this label again.
Choose a city in setup to see the qibla. Every feature still works without a location permission.
The direction from %1$s to the Kaaba in Makkah, calculated from the city\'s coordinates. It needs no permission and no network.
This device has no usable compass, so the live direction cannot be shown. The bearing above is still correct: use it with a physical compass or a known local direction.
The compass needs calibrating. Move the phone in a figure-eight until the reading settles, then hold it flat. The bearing above does not depend on the compass.
The compass reading is approximate. Hold the phone flat and away from metal.

Compass readings can be affected by nearby metal or magnets and by how the phone is held. Hold it flat. The true-north correction uses the selected city\'s position, so it is less accurate when you are far from that city.
Report a wrong time or problem

Your report goes to the app\'s operator, on the project\'s own server (Appwrite). It is used only to check the calculation behind the times you see. A wrong time is fixed in a later release, and there is no reply because the report carries no contact details.
Sending needs a connection. If it cannot be sent, the report stays on this screen so you can try again.

Only the inputs shown above, the app and calculation-library versions, your Hijri day shift, the calculated times for those dates, and anything you type below are sent. No account, name, email, device details or location history is included.
Say which time looks wrong and what you expected. Do not include personal details. Maximum length: %1$d.
Report sent. The operator reviews it against the recorded inputs.
Could not send the report. Check your connection and try again; the report is still on this screen.
